passages.text: But now listen, O Jacob My servant, Israel, whom I have chosen.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jacob.
Jacob is God's servant.
God has chosen Israel.
God tells Jacob and Israel to listen.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: This is the word of the LORD, your Maker, who formed you from the womb and who will help you: “Do not be afraid, O Jacob My servant, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is your Maker.
The LORD formed you in the womb.
The LORD will help you.
The LORD says, “Do not be afraid.”
Jacob is the LORD’s servant.
Jeshurun is the one the LORD has chosen.
passages.original: כֹּה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ אַל־ תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וִישֻׁר֖וּן בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For I will pour water on the thirsty land, and currents on the dry ground. I will pour out My Spirit on your descendants, and My blessing on your offspring.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises to act.
The LORD will pour water on the thirsty land.
The LORD will send streams on the dry ground.
The LORD will pour out His Spirit on your descendants.
The LORD will give His blessing to your offspring.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֶצָּק־ מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־ צָמֵ֔א וְנֹזְלִ֖ים עַל־ יַבָּשָׁ֑ה אֶצֹּ֤ק רוּחִי֙ עַל־ זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּבִרְכָתִ֖י עַל־ צֶאֱצָאֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: They will sprout among the grass like willows by flowing streams.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His chosen people.
God promises to bless their descendants.
Their descendants will grow strong.
They will grow up among the grass.
They will be like willows.
Willows grow by streams of water.
God will make them flourish.
passages.original: וְצָמְח֖וּ בְּבֵ֣ין חָצִ֑יר כַּעֲרָבִ֖ים עַל־ יִבְלֵי־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: One will say, ‘I belong to the LORD,’ another will call himself by the name of Jacob, and still another will write on his hand, ‘The LORD’s,’ and will take the name of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God is the King of Israel.
God is the Redeemer of Israel.
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God alone is God.
God promises to pour out His Spirit and blessing on His people’s descendants.
God’s people will respond to Him.
One person will say, “I belong to the LORD.”
Another person will call himself by the name of Jacob.
Another person will write on his hand, “The LORD’s.”
Another person will take the name of Israel.
passages.original: זֶ֤ה יֹאמַר֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אָ֔נִי וְזֶ֖ה יִקְרָ֣א בְשֵֽׁם־ יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְזֶ֗ה יִכְתֹּ֤ב יָדוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְשֵׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יְכַנֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: Thus says the LORD, the King and Redeemer of Israel, the LORD of Hosts: “I am the first and I am the last, and there is no God but Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the King of Israel.
The LORD is the Redeemer of Israel.
The LORD is the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD says, "I am the first."
The LORD says, "I am the last."
There is no God except the LORD.
No other God exists besides the LORD.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְגֹאֲל֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַ֖י אֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Who then is like Me? Let him say so! Let him declare his case before Me, since I established an ancient people. Let him foretell the things to come, and what is to take place.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the King and Redeemer of Israel.
The LORD is the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says, "Who is like Me?"
Let that person speak.
Let him declare his case before Me.
I established an ancient people.
Let him tell what will happen.
Let him announce what is to come.
Let him show the future events.
passages.original: וּמִֽי־ כָמ֣וֹנִי יִקְרָ֗א וְיַגִּידֶ֤הָ וְיַעְרְכֶ֙הָ֙ לִ֔י מִשּׂוּמִ֖י עַם־ עוֹלָ֑ם וְאֹתִיּ֛וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖אנָה יַגִּ֥ידוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not tremble or fear. Have I not told you and declared it long ago? You are My witnesses! Is there any God but Me? There is no other Rock; I know not one.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the King and Redeemer of Israel.
The LORD is the LORD of Hosts.
He speaks these words.
Do not be afraid.
Do not be terrified.
I have told you these things long ago.
I have declared them to you.
You are My witnesses.
Is there any God besides Me?
There is no other Rock.
I know of no other.
passages.original: אַֽל־ תִּפְחֲדוּ֙ וְאַל־ תִּרְה֔וּ הֲלֹ֥א מֵאָ֛ז הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י הֲיֵ֤שׁ אֱל֙וֹהַּ֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר בַּל־ יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: All makers of idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Their witnesses fail to see or comprehend, so they are put to shame.
passages.sermon:
The makers of idols are nothing.
The things they treasure are worthless.
Their witnesses do not see.
Their witnesses do not understand.
Therefore, they are put to shame.
passages.original: יֹֽצְרֵי־ פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ וַחֲמוּדֵיהֶ֖ם בַּל־ יוֹעִ֑ילוּ וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ בַּל־ יִרְא֛וּ וּבַל־ יֵדְע֖וּ לְמַ֥עַן יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: Who fashions a god or casts an idol which profits him nothing?
passages.sermon:
A person makes a god.
A person casts an idol.
This idol does not help him.
This god gives him no benefit.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל וּפֶ֣סֶל נָסָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הוֹעִֽיל׃

passages.text: Behold, all his companions will be put to shame, for the craftsmen themselves are only human. Let them all assemble and take their stand; they will all be brought to terror and shame.
passages.sermon:
All the companions of the idol maker will be put to shame.
The craftsmen who make idols are only human.
Let all these people gather together.
Let them stand up.
They will all be afraid.
They will all be put to shame together.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן כָּל־ חֲבֵרָיו֙ יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ וְחָרָשִׁ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה מֵֽאָדָ֑ם יִֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַֽעֲמֹ֔דוּ יִפְחֲד֖וּ יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: The blacksmith takes a tool and labors over the coals; he fashions an idol with hammers and forges it with his strong arms. Yet he grows hungry and loses his strength; he fails to drink water and grows faint.
passages.sermon:
A blacksmith is a person who works with metal.
He takes a tool in his hand.
He works over hot coals.
He uses hammers to shape the metal.
He makes an idol from the metal.
He uses his strong arms to forge it.
The blacksmith grows hungry as he works.
He loses his strength.
He does not stop to drink water.
He becomes weak and tired.
passages.original: חָרַ֤שׁ בַּרְזֶל֙ מַֽעֲצָ֔ד וּפָעַל֙ בַּפֶּחָ֔ם וּבַמַּקָּב֖וֹת יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיִּפְעָלֵ֙הוּ֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ כֹּח֔וֹ גַּם־ רָעֵב֙ וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֔חַ לֹא־ שָׁ֥תָה מַ֖יִם וַיִּיעָֽף׃

passages.text: The woodworker extends a measuring line; he marks it out with a stylus; he shapes it with chisels and outlines it with a compass. He fashions it in the likeness of man, like man in all his glory, that it may dwell in a shrine.
passages.sermon:
A woodworker works with wood.
He takes a measuring line and stretches it out.
He marks the wood with a stylus.
He shapes the wood using chisels.
He outlines the wood with a compass.
He makes the wood look like a man.
He gives it the appearance of a glorious person.
He prepares it to be placed in a house or shrine.
passages.original: חָרַ֣שׁ עֵצִים֮ נָ֣טָה קָו֒ יְתָאֲרֵ֣הוּ בַשֶּׂ֔רֶד יַעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ בַּמַּקְצֻע֔וֹת וּבַמְּחוּגָ֖ה יְתָאֳרֵ֑הוּ וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ כְּתַבְנִ֣ית אִ֔ישׁ כְּתִפְאֶ֥רֶת אָדָ֖ם לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: He cuts down cedars or retrieves a cypress or oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a laurel, and the rain makes it grow.
passages.sermon:
A man wants wood for his work.
He cuts down cedars.
He takes a cypress or an oak.
He chooses strong trees from the forest.
He plants a laurel tree.
Rain helps the tree grow.
passages.original: לִכְרָת־ ל֣וֹ אֲרָזִ֔ים וַיִּקַּ֤ח תִּרְזָה֙ וְאַלּ֔וֹן וַיְאַמֶּץ־ ל֖וֹ בַּעֲצֵי־ יָ֑עַר נָטַ֥ע אֹ֖רֶן וְגֶ֥שֶׁם יְגַדֵּֽל׃

passages.text: It serves as fuel for man. He takes some of it to warm himself, and he kindles a fire and bakes his bread; he even fashions it into a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.
passages.sermon:
A man uses wood as fuel.
He takes some wood to warm himself.
He kindles a fire with it.
He bakes his bread over the fire.
He also makes a god from the wood.
He worships the god he made.
He makes an idol from the wood.
He bows down to the idol.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאָדָם֙ לְבָעֵ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ וַיָּ֔חָם אַף־ יַשִּׂ֖יק וְאָ֣פָה לָ֑חֶם אַף־ יִפְעַל־ אֵל֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ עָשָׂ֥הוּ פֶ֖סֶל וַיִּסְגָּד־ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: He burns half of it in the fire, and he roasts meat on that half. He eats the roast and is satisfied. Indeed, he warms himself and says, “Ah! I am warm; I see the fire.”
passages.sermon:
A man takes a piece of wood from a tree.
He burns half of the wood in the fire.
He uses that half to roast meat.
He eats the roasted meat.
He feels satisfied.
He warms himself by the fire.
He says, “Ah! I am warm.
I see the fire.”
passages.original: חֶצְיוֹ֙ שָׂרַ֣ף בְּמוֹ־ אֵ֔שׁ עַל־ חֶצְיוֹ֙ בָּשָׂ֣ר יֹאכֵ֔ל יִצְלֶ֥ה צָלִ֖י וְיִשְׂבָּ֑ע אַף־ יָחֹם֙ וְיֹאמַ֣ר הֶאָ֔ח חַמּוֹתִ֖י רָאִ֥יתִי אֽוּר׃

passages.text: From the rest he makes a god, his graven image. He bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, “Save me, for you are my god.”
passages.sermon:
A man takes a piece of wood that remains.
He makes a god from it.
He shapes it into an idol.
He bows down to this idol.
He worships it.
He prays to it.
He says to the idol, "Save me."
He says, "You are my god."
passages.original: וּשְׁאֵ֣רִית֔וֹ לְאֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה לְפִסְל֑וֹ יִסְגּוֹד ל֤וֹ וְיִשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֔יו וְיֹאמַר֙ הַצִּילֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֵלִ֖י אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: They do not comprehend or discern, for He has shut their eyes so they cannot see and closed their minds so they cannot understand.
passages.sermon:
God acts here.
God shuts their eyes.
They cannot see.
God closes their minds.
They cannot understand.
They do not know.
They do not comprehend.
passages.original: לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ינוּ כִּ֣י טַ֤ח מֵֽרְאוֹת֙ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם מֵהַשְׂכִּ֖יל לִבֹּתָֽם׃

passages.text: And no one considers in his heart, no one has the knowledge or insight to say, “I burned half of it in the fire, and I baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and I ate. Shall I make something detestable with the rest of it? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?”
passages.sermon:
No one thinks about this in his heart.
No one has knowledge.
No one has understanding.
No one says this:
I burned half of the wood in the fire.
I baked bread on its coals.
I roasted meat and I ate it.
Should I make something disgusting from the rest of the wood?
Should I bow down to a block of wood?
passages.original: וְלֹא־ יָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־ לִבּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֨א דַ֥עַת וְלֹֽא־ תְבוּנָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ חֶצְי֞וֹ שָׂרַ֣פְתִּי בְמוֹ־ אֵ֗שׁ וְ֠אַף אָפִ֤יתִי עַל־ גֶּחָלָיו֙ לֶ֔חֶם אֶצְלֶ֥ה בָשָׂ֖ר וְאֹכֵ֑ל וְיִתְרוֹ֙ לְתוֹעֵבָ֣ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה לְב֥וּל עֵ֖ץ אֶסְגּֽוֹד׃

passages.text: He feeds on ashes. His deluded heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver himself or say, “Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?”
passages.sermon:
This man feeds on ashes.
His heart is deceived.
His heart leads him astray.
He cannot save himself.
He does not say, “Is this thing in my right hand a lie?”
passages.original: רֹעֶ֣ה אֵ֔פֶר לֵ֥ב הוּתַ֖ל הִטָּ֑הוּ וְלֹֽא־ יַצִּ֤יל אֶת־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יֹאמַ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא שֶׁ֖קֶר בִּימִינִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Remember these things, O Jacob, for you are My servant, O Israel. I have made you, and you are My servant; O Israel, I will never forget you.
passages.sermon:
Jacob, remember these things.
Israel, you are My servant.
I made you.
You are My servant.
Israel, I will never forget you.
passages.original: זְכָר־ אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי־ אָ֑תָּה יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד־ לִי֙ אַ֔תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א תִנָּשֵֽׁנִי׃

passages.text: I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God says, “I have removed your sins.
I have wiped away your transgressions like a cloud.
I have cleared away your sins like a mist.
Return to Me.
I have redeemed you.”
passages.original: מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ וְכֶעָנָ֖ן חַטֹּאותֶ֑יךָ שׁוּבָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Sing for joy, O heavens, for the LORD has done this; shout aloud, O depths of the earth. Break forth in song, O mountains, you forests and all your trees. For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and revealed His glory in Israel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Redeemer of Jacob.
The LORD has shown His glory in Israel.
He has acted with power and mercy.
He has saved His people.
Heavens, sing for joy.
Depths of the earth, shout aloud.
Mountains, break forth in song.
Forests and every tree, rejoice.
The LORD has done this great work.
He has redeemed Jacob.
He has revealed His glory in Israel.
passages.original: רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי־ עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הָרִ֙יעוּ֙ תַּחְתִּיּ֣וֹת אָ֔רֶץ פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה יַ֖עַר וְכָל־ עֵ֣ץ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ גָאַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְפָּאָֽר׃פ

passages.text: Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer who formed you from the womb: “I am the LORD, who has made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth, who foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense, who confirms the message of His servant and fulfills the counsel of His messengers, who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be inhabited,’ and of the cities of Judah, ‘They will be rebuilt, and I will restore their ruins,’ who says to the depths of the sea, ‘Be dry, and I will dry up your currents,’ who says of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire,’ who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be rebuilt,’ and of the temple, ‘Let its foundation be laid.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your Redeemer.
The LORD formed you in the womb.
The LORD says these words.
The LORD made all things.
The LORD alone stretched out the heavens.
The LORD alone spread out the earth.
No one was with the LORD when He did this.
The LORD destroys the signs of false prophets.
The LORD makes diviners act like fools.
The LORD confounds the wise.
The LORD turns their knowledge into nonsense.
The LORD confirms the words of His servant.
The LORD fulfills the plans of His messengers.
The LORD says about Jerusalem, “She will be inhabited.”
The LORD says about the cities of Judah, “They will be rebuilt.”
The LORD says, “I will restore their ruins.”
The LORD says to the deep sea, “Be dry.”
The LORD says, “I will dry up your rivers.”
The LORD says about Cyrus, “He is My shepherd.”
Cyrus will carry out all the LORD’s purpose.
The LORD says about Jerusalem, “She will be rebuilt.”
The LORD says about the temple, “Let its foundation be laid.”
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן אָנֹכִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עֹ֣שֶׂה כֹּ֔ל נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ לְבַדִּ֔י רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ מִי אִתִּי׃ מֵפֵר֙ אֹת֣וֹת בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֹסְמִ֖ים יְהוֹלֵ֑ל מֵשִׁ֧יב חֲכָמִ֛ים אָח֖וֹר וְדַעְתָּ֥ם יְשַׂכֵּֽל׃ מֵקִים֙ דְּבַ֣ר עַבְדּ֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֥ת מַלְאָכָ֖יו יַשְׁלִ֑ים הָאֹמֵ֨ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם תּוּשָׁ֗ב וּלְעָרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ינָה וְחָרְבוֹתֶ֖יהָ אֲקוֹמֵֽם׃ הָאֹמֵ֥ר לַצּוּלָ֖ה חֳרָ֑בִי וְנַהֲרֹתַ֖יִךְ אוֹבִֽישׁ׃ הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֙וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י וְכָל־ חֶפְצִ֖י יַשְׁלִ֑ם וְלֵאמֹ֤ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ה וְהֵיכָ֖ל תִּוָּסֵֽד׃ס
